chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Kulaib al-Asadi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) over the deceased.
He said with his hand (indicating) five.
I said: So how should I say it when I pray over him?

He said: You say, 'O Allah, Your servant has need of Your mercy, and You are free of need of his punishment. O Allah, if he was a doer of good, increase in his goodness, and if he was a doer of evil, forgive him.'

key_terms.اَلتَّكْبِيرِ: Saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), a ritual act in prayer
key_terms.غَنِيٌّ عَنْ: Free of need of / Independent of

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication to recite during the funeral prayer according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the canonical formula for the funeral supplication, emphasizing the dual nature of the deceased's status as either an *muhsin* (doer of good) or *mu'sin* (doer of evil). The Imam’s instruction reflects the Shia juristic principle of conditional supplication, where the prayer covers both possibilities to ensure comprehensive mercy, aligning with the theological balance between divine justice and grace.
